userStories.title: Capacity weighted by what a job costs
userStories.description: A slot is one job whatever its cost: a near-free copy, a paused job and a 4K tone-mapped encode (3.2 cores) each take one, so PlaybackInfo refuses with every slot busy while processors idle, and two 4K jobs overcommit a small worker. Workers declare cores; a job's cost comes from its spec using the measured table in docs/transcoding.md; copies and paused jobs count near zero under a separate I/O bound. Closes BL-034; precedes JS-054 and JS-057.
acceptanceCriteria: A worker's cores are worker configuration, documented in docs/transcoding.md: a negative value is refused at startup as transcodeSlots is, and a config that declares none (or still sets transcodeSlots) starts and its worker still takes re-encodes

A job's cost is fixed by what it does to which source and is the same on every replica and worker: 0.8 cores to re-encode a 1080p SDR source, 1.6 for 4K SDR, 2.0 for 1080p tone-mapped, 3.2 for 4K tone-mapped (the table in docs/transcoding.md), and near zero, at a figure the docs state, for a copy whether its audio is copied or re-encoded
A 4K source costs its 4K figure although its output is at most 1080 lines, a source taller than 1080 lines never costs less than the 1080p figure, and a helper costs what the job it helps costs

PlaybackInfo offers a transcode whenever some worker of the viewer's output version has the job's cost free: shown on one worker holding more copies than transcodeSlots admitted (2 by default), some reading and some paused at their lead, where a re-encode is offered, claimed and makes its first segment
Costs that add up to exactly a worker's cores fit: a 4-core worker holding four 1080p SDR re-encodes is offered and takes a fifth, and one holding a 4K tone-mapped re-encode takes a 1080p SDR one

PlaybackInfo refuses, with jellyfin-web's "cannot be played at this time" dialog within seconds, when no single worker has the cost free, also when the workers' free cores add up to more than the cost (two 4-core workers each holding a 2.0 re-encode refuse a 3.2 one); the log line gives the job's cost and says cores are short, and does not speak of slots

The count keeps what slot counting has today: only live workers and jobs of the replica's output version count, the asking viewer's own jobs and helpers do not, several viewers of one spec cost one job, and a spec with a live job is offered whatever is free
A job queued and not yet claimed counts against capacity: with one 4-core worker and a 4K tone-mapped job queued, a second viewer's 4K tone-mapped PlaybackInfo is refused

A worker never holds jobs whose costs add up to more than its cores: with two 4K tone-mapped re-encodes queued at the same moment for one 4-core worker, one runs, and the other starts no ffmpeg, waits queueTimeout (6 s) and is answered 503 as an untaken job is today, the log saying cores were short and not that no worker runs

That holds when the first is paused at its lead as the second arrives, when the second is a dead worker's job failing over, and with helpers counted; PlaybackInfo's answer does not change with whether a watched re-encode happens to be paused at that moment

With two 4-core workers and the same two jobs, each worker runs one; a worker with too few cores free for the oldest queued job leaves it for a worker that has them and claims at once, not when it expires, a later job that fits
A job that costs more than the cores of every live worker is refused at PlaybackInfo, and the log gives the job's cost and the most cores any worker has

Copies are bounded apart from cores by a count per worker: at the bound that worker takes no further copy and PlaybackInfo refuses one when every worker is at its bound, the log naming that bound, while a re-encode the cores have room for is still offered and taken

A new viewer never waits behind helpers: when their job fits a worker only once helpers stop, PlaybackInfo offers it and as many helpers as it takes on one worker are stopped, several if one is not enough and never a viewer's job; a helper is neither queued nor claimed where it would put a worker over its cores

The queue signal KEDA will scale on is in cores: the sum of the costs of the jobs queued and not past queueTimeout, for the whole cluster, so one queued 4K tone-mapped job reads 3.2, one queued 1080p SDR job 0.8, both together 4.0 and an empty queue 0

The number of queued jobs stays readable beside it, so copies held back by their own bound are not read as no demand, and each worker reports the cores it declared and the cost of the jobs it holds where it reported slots and slots busy; docs/running.md names the metrics

Replicas and workers roll in any order: beside a worker of the release before (a row with slots and no cores) or a job queued by a replica of the release before, a viewer's re-encode is still offered, claimed and counted at a cost above zero
docs/transcoding.md (sizing a worker, the reasons for the dialog), DOMAINS.md where 37, 53, 57, 58 and 59 speak of slots, and ARCHITECTURE.md rule 3 and its roles table say what is now true

userStories.title: A film recovers from a failed segment without the viewer acting
userStories.description: A failed segment, a wrong keyframe index and a failed burn-in each freeze the film mid-play today, because jellyfin-web drops the stream on a segment error after playback has begun. The owner asked (2026-11-12) for recovery without the viewer acting, for example falling back from copy to re-encode at the same position. Observe first how jellyfin-web and an ExoPlayer client react to a segment error.
acceptanceCriteria: Observed in the e2e tier, jellyfin-web 12.4 (its bundled hls.js 1.6.16) in Chromium, after playback has begun, given one segment answered 500, one answered 404, one with no first byte for over 10 s, and one whose connection closes mid-body: for each, how many times it asks again, whether it asks PlaybackInfo again, whether a dialog shows and whether the picture goes on. Recorded beside the other captures, with the scenario that reproduces it
The same four cases are recorded for one named ExoPlayer (Media3) version from its source, citing the file and line for each, and marked not observed

A copy whose keyframe index is found wrong goes on as a re-encode in jellyfin-web in the e2e tier, with no dialog, no request answered 400 or more, no request abandoned, and currentTime reaching 30 s past the bad point. This holds when the viewer reaches the bad segment and also when the job finds it while the viewer is still playing stored copy segments before it
The re-encode goes on at the viewer's position: currentTime never goes back by more than one 4 s segment (so never to 0 or the resume point) and never skips forward by more than 1 s
After the fallback the viewer keeps the audio track and the subtitle track they had chosen
Two viewers playing the same copy when its index is found wrong both go on as re-encodes, as in the third criterion
Each fallback from copy to re-encode is in the operator's log (item, source and reason) and in a metric that counts once per stream that falls back, not once per segment

A copy job that fails for a cause that is not the file's (the transcode store refusing a put, the source store cutting a read, its ffmpeg killed by a signal) is made again as a copy. Its keyframe index is kept and no re-encode starts (invariant 45)

A segment whose job failed for a cause that is not the file's (the same three causes) is made by a fresh job and answered to the request that was waiting on it, with no error status and within 10 s of the request when the job failed at its first segment. This holds for a re-encode, a copy and a job that burns in a subtitle
When two requests (two viewers, or two stream replicas) are both waiting on a job as it fails, they start one fresh job between them, not two. The check makes both requests wait before the failure

A recovered failure stays visible: the job is recorded failed with its cause and counted in jellyscale_transcode_jobs_ended_total{result="failed"}, and it refuses neither the spec's later segment requests nor its PlaybackInfo
A cause that persists starts at most 3 fresh jobs (maxRestarts) for one request. The request then gets the documented failure that names the cause (JS-107), never an endless series of jobs

A failure that is the file's (ffmpeg failing on the file's own data, or the input ending early as in invariant 40) starts no fresh job of the spec within failureMemory (30 s), as today. It is answered with the failure and refuses the spec
userStories.notes: Built 2026-11-17, partly in OpenCode after Claude Code's weekly limit: refine and check on Opus 5.5, spec, build and fix on Sonnet 5.5, verify on Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, re-review on Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5. jellyfin-web 12.4 observed in the e2e tier (compat/captures/segment-errors-12.4.md): after playback has begun a 500 or 404 on a segment ends the stream with no dialog and no new PlaybackInfo, while a stalled or cut request is asked again; ExoPlayer (Media3 1.5.1) read from source, not observed (JS-075). A job that fails for a cause that is not the file's is made again for the waiting request, at most three times per spec within failureMemory across requests; only a store failure the Reader gave up on counts (store.InputWithFailure). A copy whose index is found wrong goes on as an x264 or x265 encode cut on the playlist's layout (dropped_keyframes, Spec.Recode), capped at 1080 lines, priced from a measurement, each segment led by its own init; OutputVersion 5. The lead settled three disputed checks (the rig's film size, the HEVC length measure, a PlaybackInfo jellyfin-web never sends). Not built: AV1 fallback (SVT-AV1 exists but no restart-safe AV1 encode), a fallback while Postgres is away.

userStories.title: A seek into a long-showing image subtitle costs no more than any seek
userStories.description: JS-071 draws the cue showing at a seek by decoding the film from the cue's start: about 0.3 MB and 0.04 s per second of the cue's age, uncapped (BL-049). The owner wants that cost gone (2026-11-12). Extract each image track once into a subtitle-only file in the asset store, as text tracks are, and burn in from it as a second input with the film itself seeked to the cut, so the cue's age costs kilobytes. Starts with a spike: ffmpeg 6.1's timestamp alignment of the two inputs.
acceptanceCriteria: With a film's image track stored (by a worker's extraction asked for as a client's playback asks, never put in the asset store by the test), a seek into a showing PGS, VobSub or DVB cue reads no more of the film before its first segment than the same seek without the track, within the spread of repeated runs, through a worker's job on a film the scan has read; shown for a cue 8 s old, one 56 s old (DVB: 56 s if the kit can write such a cue, else its longest, 24 s in JS-071's kit) and one that is never cleared, and the older cue's read is not above the younger's
The same bound holds for a failover restart and a helper's chunk that begin inside the 56 s cue

What such a run reads for the cue instead comes from the asset store: before its first segment at most the stored track once, the same for a cue 8 s and 56 s old, and nothing that grows with the film's length

With the track stored, every run that begins mid-film (a seek, a failover restart, a helper's chunk) draws what a run from zero draws at and after its cut: the showing cue from its first frame until it ends, nothing in a gap between cues, before the first or after the last, the later of two cues, and a PGS picture built by two packets whole; for PGS, VobSub, DVB, a PGS remux with compressed blocks and MPEG-2 with VobSub

A cue drawn from the stored track is the picture a run from zero draws: the same place, size and colours (VobSub's palette, each track's canvas), compared on the pixels and not only on where bright pixels fall

A cue drawn from the stored track appears and ends on the same video frame as in a run from zero, compared frame by frame at both edges and not once a second, for a film whose clock starts at zero and one whose does not (MPEG-TS), under ffmpeg 6.1 (test/ffmpeg61.sh, as CI) and ffmpeg 9

Every segment a run makes with the stored track has the same number of video frames at the same times (within 1 ms) as a run from zero's (invariant 22); shown for one spec whose earlier segments were made before the track was stored and its later ones after, with the cue unbroken across the seam

On a film that lists no cue points for the track (MPEG-TS; Matroska with no Cues, or with Cues for the video only), once the track is stored a mid-film run draws a cue older than the 10 s look-back from its first frame and reads no more of the film than the same run without the track; until it is stored the look-back and its miss are as JS-071 left them

No transcode job (from zero, a seek, a failover, a helper) waits for the extraction or starts a read that grows with the film's length: while the track is not stored (never asked for, being extracted, failed) a run makes its first segment within JS-071's read bounds and draws JS-071's pictures; shown with an extraction held in the middle of its read

A viewer's play of a film with an image track burnt, through the requests a client makes (PlaybackInfo, the playlists, segments), gets every image track inside the film stored with no other request and no step by the operator, also for a film the previous release scanned and without a new scan

A scan starts no extraction, and neither does a play that burns no image track: direct play, a text track, a PGS track the client draws, an image file beside the film (which is burnt as today and reads nothing it does not read today)

The extraction is one worker job and one read of the film, however many viewers ask at once, through two api replicas and with two workers running (a seek and a helper at once among them), and however many image tracks the film has (two PGS tracks; PGS with VobSub): the film's store serves the film at most once for it, and each track draws its own cues, never another track's

Once stored, a later play, a pick of the film's other image track, a seek, a failover and a helper's chunk start no extraction and read nothing of the film for the track, on any worker and after every worker has restarted

An extraction that ends for a reason that is not the film's (a store error or timeout mid-read, its worker killed, its lease lost, a graceful stop) stores nothing, never a track cut short, is not remembered as the film's, and is taken up again as a text track's is (invariant 43: another worker within about a second of a kill); runs meanwhile draw as JS-071 does

A film whose image track cannot be extracted for a reason that is the film's keeps the track listed and burnt by every run as JS-071 burns it, is not read again for that track until its file changes, and its other image tracks are stored all the same (at most a second read of the film, as the text pass)

A run that cannot read the stored track for a reason that is not the film's (the asset store fails or times out, the object is gone) stores no segment without a cue a run from zero draws, is not remembered as the film's failure, and its read ends with its job

After a film's file is replaced by one whose cues fall at other times, with the old file's track stored, a mid-film run draws and reads by the new file's cues and never from the old file's track, and the new file is read once for its own
The asset sweep removes the stored track of a replaced file's previous version and of a removed film (JS-078's check, with this asset beside subtitle text, .sup copies and images)
The asset sweep never removes the stored track of a current file: not one put after the sweep listed the store, and not while the film's extraction is queued or running

In jellyfin-web a viewer playing a film with a burnt PGS track seeks into a cue that began 50 s or more earlier, after that playback's own requests have had the track stored: the cue is on screen at the first frame played after the seek and until it ends, the segment came from a run that drew from the stored track, and the player reports no error
Every JS-071 check still passes, none edited (internal/transcode/image_burn_*_test.go, its docs checks, its e2e scenario)

DOMAINS 51, ARCHITECTURE's Known departures, docs/status.md and docs/running.md (what the sweep removes) agree and state what the stored track costs per film (one read of the whole film, its bytes in the asset store, one job row) and per run, when a cue's age still costs film reads (until the track is stored, or when it cannot be) and the rollout order; docs/transcoding.md records what the spike found of the two inputs' alignment on ffmpeg 6.1 and 9, and a seek's bytes read and time to first segment with no cue showing and inside a cue 8 s and 50 s old, for origin/main, this build before the track is stored and after; no check passes or fails on a duration
userStories.notes: Built 2026-11-19 under decisions D-002 (time limit), D-003 (one whole-film read per file version) and D-004 (the JS-071 count).

userStories.title: A subtitle track ffmpeg hangs on no longer costs the film's other tracks
userStories.description: JS-028 extracts every text track in one ffmpeg run, so a track that hangs until the time limit leaves the film's good tracks unstored (Changed guarantees of #83). The owner wants that cost gone (2026-11-12): only when a run is killed by the limit and names no stream, fall back to one run per track; store the good ones and mark unreadable a track that times out alone. Add a stall limit (no output growth for about 60 s) so a hang is found in a minute, not at the extraction limit.
acceptanceCriteria: A film with one text track ffmpeg hangs on (first, middle or last of its text tracks; whichever track is asked for first) has every other text track stored under its own index with its own text in every format and served 200 by stream, and the request that queued the job is the one answered: no second ask is needed.

The same holds for several bad tracks in one film: with two hanging tracks, or one hanging and one ffmpeg refuses to decode, every remaining text track is stored and served and each bad one is marked unreadable.

A pass ended by a limit is followed, in the same job, by at most one run per text track not yet stored, one ffmpeg at a time (so a worker still runs at most four extractions at once), no track run alone twice: at most 1 + n ffmpeg runs for a film of n text tracks, or 2 + n when the pass first named a stream.

A track whose own run is ended by a limit, while another run of that fallback ran to its end, is marked unreadable as an undecodable track is: it leaves the listing on every replica, and a request for it answers 500 "could not be read" at once with no job and no ffmpeg run, also after the 30 s failure memory; the film's good tracks are then served from the store with no job.

When no run of the fallback runs to its end (every track's run is ended by a limit, as when the store stalls without an error, or the film has a single text track), no track whose run was ended by a limit is marked (a track ffmpeg's decoder refused in a run that read the film is still marked, as criterion 1 asks, also in a film of two text tracks): the job fails as a failure that may pass, not as unreadable, is remembered for the failure memory, and the next ask after it runs the film again.

An ffmpeg that does nothing for the stall limit (about 60 s by default), in the pass or in a single-track run, is ended by the stall limit and the next run starts at once: with the extraction limit left at its hour, the job of a film with a hanging track still ends, after about two stall limits and the reads of its good tracks.

A run that is still reading the film is never ended by the stall limit, however long it writes nothing: a film that takes several stall limits to read, whose cues are further apart than the limit and whose tracks ffmpeg writes out only when it ends, is read once and every track is stored.

A film without a hanging track is still read once: one ffmpeg run for all its text tracks, on POSIX and on S3; a film whose bad tracks ffmpeg names is still read at most twice with no single-track run; a file ffmpeg can't open is still read once with none.

A pass ended by the extraction limit rather than the stall limit falls back the same way, and every run of the fallback has the whole extraction limit and a stall limit of its own, never what an earlier run left.

Only a limit that ends a run starts the fallback or marks a track: a run ended by a store that refuses or cuts a read, a store write that fails or never returns, a signal, a full disk, the worker shutting down, or a lease lost or not renewed starts no further run and marks nothing, and the job ends as it does today (failed and remembered 30 s, put back in the queue, or left to its new owner).

The job keeps its lease from the pass through its last fallback run, which lasts longer than a lease: with two workers and two api replicas asking for a good and the hanging track at the same moment there is one job, claimed once (attempts 1), one pass and one fallback in all, the good track answered with its text and the hanging one as unreadable.

A worker killed during the stalled pass or during a fallback run (its ffmpeg dies with it) has the job claimed by another worker before its lease would have run out, and that worker leaves the good tracks stored and the hanging one marked; a lease lost after the third claim still fails the row for good, and a worker that loses its lease mid-fallback starts no further run.

A fallback over a version of the film that is replaced meanwhile marks nothing on the new version, and a replaced film (a new ETag) is read afresh by a pass of its own, with the old version's mark gone.

Jobs other than the film's text pass (a subtitle file beside the film, .sup, fonts, chapter pictures) behave as before, a timeout there still marking nothing, and every JS-028 and JS-030 subtitle check still passes, except that the check of a pass whose first run alone outlasts the limit is restated for the fallback, its guarantee kept by the criteria above.

docs/subtitles.md and DOMAINS invariants 43 and 50 state the fallback and its cost in reads, the stall limit and its default, and which timeouts mark a track and which do not, and no longer say a hanging track costs the film's other tracks.

userStories.title: Find and fix the recurring CI flakes
userStories.description: Recurring failures with no known cause: the POSIX burn-in of PGS (and VobSub) after far seeks in the subtitles e2e gate (the video element null, or playback stalled past 22 s; 3 queue runs, 2 PRs, and locally); and an ffprobe 'Stream ends prematurely' in a fault-injection test of PR 96. Hunt each under CI's cpuset with E2E_REPEAT or -count, decide whether it is a product race or a test bug, and fix the cause; never by a retry or a skip.
acceptanceCriteria: Each named failure is first tied to what failed: the record (docs/testing.md) names the scenario or test, the failing line and its message, and a CI or local run that shows it, and tells a check that failed from a line a passing test logs. The named ones are the subtitles gate's 'POSIX burn-in of PGS for a viewer whose client doesn't draw it ... after far seeks' and 'POSIX burn-in of VobSub: ... after far seeks' with their two symptoms (the video element null: `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'seeking')` in seek; the stall: `timed out waiting for playback past 22` in seeCue), and the ffprobe `Stream ends prematurely` line of TestAFailedReadOfTheCueTimesNeverLeavesASegmentWithoutTheCue (internal/transcode/image_burn_failures_integration_test.go:138)

Each burn-in symptom is reproduced at least once, or the two scenarios pass 20 of 20 runs, with test/e2e/run.sh under `taskset -c` on four CPUs, E2E_GATES=subtitles and E2E_ONLY matching only those two scenarios (one command for both, never a whole gate or tier); other work on the machine may run meanwhile, and a failure seen only under that load counts as reproduced. The record gives the command, the CPU list, the ffmpeg version and `passed p of n` per scenario

A 'does not reproduce' counts only runs that take the path CI's failing run took, the film's first burn-in on a fresh stack: 20 fresh stacks, unless the record names what a first burn-in stores that a later run reads and shows E2E_REPEAT's reset removes it (or that it stores nothing), in which case 20 warm iterations count

Each recorded cause is a mechanism shown by the failing run's own evidence (its FAIL line, the requests the player made in those seconds with their answers, the server's and worker's log lines for the job), and says product race or test bug: for the null video element, what took the player's video away between the seek being set and a later poll; for the stall, which segment the player waited for and what the job and its ffmpeg run did about it. If one cause explains both symptoms the record shows each from it; a cause not found in 20 runs is recorded as not found, with what was ruled out, never as a guess

The ffprobe line: if no CI run shows its test failing (the line is the logged outcome of the Open the test fails on purpose), the record says so with the runs and the line, the test passes 20 of 20 with `-run` and `-count=20` under `taskset -c` on four CPUs, and no fix or test is owed for it; if a CI run or one of the 20 shows the test failing with it, it is hunted, explained and fixed as the burn-in failures are

Each cause found has a test that forces the condition that caused it (the order of events, the answer, the moment of the seek) and does not wait for it by repeating: it fails on each of 3 runs without the fix and passes on each of 3 with it, whether the fix is in the product or in a test helper; a race between processes is forced with real processes

No fix is a retry of a failed step, scenario or test, a skip, or a loosened check: the burn-in scenarios still check the bar's place at each of the four cue points, a run restarted before the first cue, no subtitle job for a track inside the film, no subtitle file fetched and no page error or 5xx, and a player that left the film or was answered an error while it should be playing still fails them. A fix to a helper that other scenarios share is made in the helper, not around it in the two named scenarios
After the fix, the command that reproduced each failure passes every run of 20 on four CPUs, or of three times the number of runs the failure took to show once if that is more

Languages compare by language, not spelling: ger, deu, de, de-DE and GER are one; fre, fra and fr are one; chi, zho and zh are one; pt-br and por are one; nor, nob and nno are one; zho, cmn and yue are one; eng and deu differ; eng and enm differ
A tag with no language equals nothing, itself included: the empty tag, und, mis, mul, zxx, and a tag that does not parse (a test fails if und or an unparseable tag compares equal to eng)

userStories.title: A client changes one setting without overwriting the rest
userStories.description: Jellyfin's POST /Users/Configuration replaces the whole Configuration (compat/captures/user-configuration-12.4.md), so a client reads it, changes a field and posts everything back, and two apps saving close together undo each other (issue #159, from Fluster). PATCH /jellyscale/v1/users/configuration changes only the fields its body names, merged in one statement onto what is stored, so no client that uses it overwrites a field it did not name. Jellyfin's two routes stay as JS-116 built them.
acceptanceCriteria: PATCH /jellyscale/v1/users/configuration with a JSON object naming any of the 15 savable fields of UserConfiguration changes exactly those fields for the caller and answers 200 with the whole Configuration as GET /Users/Me then answers it. For each of the 15 in turn, starting from a document with all 15 changed from their defaults, a body with that one field leaves the other 14 as they were, read through GET /Users/Me on a second api process and again after both restart
A viewer who has saved nothing and patches one field reads that field and the new user's value for the other 14 (AudioLanguagePreference absent); {} answers 200 with the document and changes nothing

One parser with POST /Users/Configuration: every value the capture shows accepted for a field is accepted here and reads back the same (SubtitleMode 'always' and 1 read back 'Always'; a dashed upper-case id reads back compact; AudioLanguagePreference '' reads back ''), and every value it shows refused is 400 here

400 naming the field, and nothing stored: an unknown field, CastReceiverId, null for any field, a value of the wrong type, a SubtitleMode outside the enum, a list entry that is not an id. 400 and nothing stored: a body that is not a JSON object, an empty body, a body over 64 KB. A body with one good field and one refused field stores neither
The caller only: the route takes no user id, an administrator's PATCH changes the administrator's settings alone, a second viewer's 16 fields are as they were, and no token answers 401

Forced, different fields: the test holds the viewer's users row (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE in an open transaction), sends PATCH {SubtitleMode: 'Always'} through one api process and PATCH {AudioLanguagePreference: 'deu'} through another, waits until pg_stat_activity shows two statements waiting on a lock, and commits. Both answer 200 and GET /Users/Me has both changes with the other 13 fields untouched. Forced, against Jellyfin's save: the PATCH {AudioLanguagePreference: 'deu'} statement is held at the database proxy (testenv.DBProxy.OnStatement) after its request authenticated; a full-body POST /Users/Configuration that sets SubtitleLanguagePreference 'fra' and carries the old audio language answers 204; the held statement is released. The result is the POST's 15 fields with AudioLanguagePreference 'deu'

The limit, as a test: a full-body POST built from a read taken before a PATCH, sent after it, wins whole, as on Jellyfin 12.4
No Jellyfin route answers differently: JS-116's replay of the 124 captured cases passes unchanged and the differential tier passes with no new entry in compat/differences.yaml

A change is logged at Info with the user id and the names of the fields sent. The route is in compat/endpoints.yaml, in the jellyscale-only list of compat/coverage_test.go, and in compat/conform.yaml with its answer held to UserConfiguration's schema. docs/api.md documents it with a request and an answer, how a concurrent save of the same field is decided, and that a whole-object save from an older read (jellyfin-web's) can still undo a change while the track preferences are out of its reach

userStories.title: Every route declares who may call it, and one test holds each to it
userStories.description: Who may call a route is decided today by a Public flag in routes.go that the generated manifest does not show, and by checks written inside handlers. Media already requires a token (server.go requireAuth), but nothing pins it: one changed line opens a film to anyone, and TestProtectedRoutesRejectAnonymousRequests asks four routes. The owner's rule (2026-11-16) is that playback and personal data always require authorization, with no compatibility exception. This task makes the declaration explicit and required, prints it in compat/endpoints.yaml, documents it, and asks every route. No answer changes.
acceptanceCriteria: Route has Access, 'anyone' or 'viewer', in place of Public. A route with no Access fails go test ./internal/api naming the route, and Server.Handler() panics on it, so the binary does not start. An 'anyone' route has a non-empty Why and a 'viewer' route has none; a test fails on either. jellyscale --print-routes writes access: for every route and TestManifestIsCurrent holds compat/endpoints.yaml to it

The open list is pinned by a test that names it: GET /System/Info/Public, GET and POST /System/Ping, GET /Branding/Configuration, GET /Branding/Css, GET /Branding/Css.css, GET /QuickConnect/Enabled, GET /Users/Public, POST /Users/AuthenticateByName, and, by the owner's decision on pictures, GET /Items/{itemId}/Images/{imageType} and GET /Items/{itemId}/Images/{imageType}/{imageIndex}. The other 77 routes are 'viewer'. Adding or removing an open route fails the test until its list is changed

TestAccess (integration tier, Postgres, both stores, the synthetic films with a text subtitle, a font and chapter pictures) asks every route of Routes(), 88 or more, on a handler with roles api and stream, and each role's routes again on a handler with that role alone. Path wildcards are filled by name from the fixtures, and a wildcard the test has no value for fails it naming the route

For every 'viewer' route the answer is 401 with the body 'unauthorized' and under 64 bytes, with no Content-Range, Content-Disposition, ETag or Location header, for: no token; an unknown token in each of the seven spellings compat.ParseAuth reads (Authorization MediaBrowser, Authorization Emby, X-Emby-Authorization, X-Emby-Token, X-MediaBrowser-Token, ApiKey, api_key); a token signed out through POST /Sessions/Logout; the token of a user deleted from the users table. HEAD of each GET route and the path in upper case with a trailing slash answer the same
For every 'anyone' route the same requests answer neither 401 nor 403

With a valid token in each of the seven spellings, GET /Videos/{itemId}/stream?static=true with Range bytes=0-9 answers 206 with the film's first ten bytes, and every 'viewer' route answers as it does today: the unit, integration, roles, e2e and differential tiers pass with no test changed except the one this task replaces, and compat/differences.yaml gains no entry
The mux serves nothing outside Routes() except GET /healthz, GET /readyz, GET /web/ and GET /; a test fails on any other registered pattern

Forced, real processes (test/roles.sh: two api processes and a stream process): a token signed in through api 1 gets 206 for a byte range from stream; POST /Sessions/Logout through api 1 answers 204; the very next request with that token through api 2 (GET /Users/Me) and through stream (the byte range) answers 401, with no retry. Named mutant, which must fail every run: tokens remembered in the process for 5 seconds

Forced, the snapshot never decides while Postgres answers: a session reports Playing, the test waits until the stream replica's snapshot holds its token (the hook the outage tests use), the token is signed out, and its byte range answers 401. Named mutant, which must fail every run: a Snapshot route served from the snapshot before Postgres is asked

With Postgres held away (testenv.DBProxy): every 'viewer' route asked with no token answers 401 within 1 second; a Snapshot route asked with an unknown token sends no byte while Postgres is away and answers 401 once it is back
Named mutants, each failing TestAccess on every run: GET /Videos/{itemId}/{file} declared 'anyone'; the guard accepting any non-empty token; a new Route with an empty Access

docs/access.md (new, linked from README and DOMAINS.md) holds the model and one table row per served route: what it does, who it requires and its scope. A test fails when a route of compat/endpoints.yaml has no row, a row names no route, or a row's 'requires' cell differs from the manifest

DOMAINS.md gains a Security invariant: every route declares its access; none is open by default; media, item data and anything naming a user are never open; an open route says why. docs/status.md says a client must send its token on every media request and that this is stricter than Jellyfin on purpose. The sentence proposed for PRODUCT.md's compatibility policy is in the pull request's description, not in the file
userStories.notes: Owner, 2026-11-16: playback and personal data always require authorization; compatibility never means copying Jellyfin's openings. Media already answers 401 with no token, so this task changes no answer. 'admin' joins Access with its first route in JS-033. The draft's compat/anonymous.yaml is dropped: Route.Access is the one source. Pictures: jellyfin-web builds picture URLs with no token (web-dist/node_modules.jellyfin-apiclient.bundle.js, getImageUrl) and an cannot send one, so a token on pictures removes every poster; item ids are random (internal/library/scan.go). If the owner decides pictures need a token, that is its own task and the pinned list here has nine routes. Found while reading, for the backlog: two sign-ins at once with one DeviceId can leave two tokens for the device (users.go:107-117, no unique index on user_id, device_id); a viewer sees the worker's name in their own TranscodingInfo (transcoding_info.go:69-70). Owner's decisions (2026-11-16, on Fable 5.2's access model, .results/access-model-fable-2026-11-16.md): pictures by id open to whoever holds the id, by name need a token; per-library access right after JS-033; a revoked or disabled user's running stream stops within 15 s; a viewer sees no other viewer's name; an administrator manages accounts but never browses, plays or reports as another user; a Policy field jellyscale does not enforce is refused when changed (400); 'may download' is honoured; operator keys are never users; no issue is filed on Findroid for now.

userStories.title: What Jellyfin opens and jellyscale does not: observed, listed, and each client's player held to it
userStories.description: Jellyfin 12.4's source shows no authorization on the video stream, subtitle and font routes (VideosController.cs:314, SubtitleController.cs:215 and 303, VideoAttachmentsController.cs:50 at tag v12.4), and lets any signed-in user read every account (UserController.cs:91 and 127). None of that has been observed on a running server, and nobody has listed which clients depend on it. Findroid does: its direct-play URL carries no token. This task observes Jellyfin, records each difference as an improvement, and reads what each client's player really sends, so that 'this client needs to send its token' is a fact with a source.
acceptanceCriteria: Observed first: compat/captures/access-12.4.md and .json record, from a real jellyfin/jellyfin:12.4 with the synthetic films (a film, an episode, a text and an image subtitle, a font, chapter pictures), an administrator and a non-administrator: for every route in compat/endpoints.yaml, the status with no token, with an unknown token, and with the non-administrator's token; for the media routes, whether the body held the file's bytes. The capture lists the routes Jellyfin answers 2xx or 3xx with no token, and the routes it refuses the non-administrator

The differential tier can send a request with no token (a field of the request in test/differential/requests.yaml) and compares the status. It asks both servers, with no token: GET and HEAD /Videos/{film}/stream?static=true, GET /Videos/{film}/stream.mkv, the text subtitle as Stream.vtt with and without a start offset, the font attachment, GET /Videos/{film}/master.m3u8, GET /Items/{film}/Download, GET /Items/{film}, GET /Items/{film}/Images/Primary, GET /Users/Public and GET /System/Info/Public

Each of those where Jellyfin answers 2xx and jellyscale 401 is one entry in compat/differences.yaml of kind improvement, naming the request and the reason. A no-token request whose statuses differ with no entry fails the tier

Never looser: a no-token request that jellyscale answers 2xx or 3xx and Jellyfin answers 401 or 403 fails the tier, and no kind of entry allows it. A test of the tier shows this with a made-up pair of answers

compat/clients.yaml gains, for Findroid, Android TV, Swiftfin and Streamyfin, a 'player' path: the direct-play request, the HLS master request, a subtitle request and a picture request as the client builds them, read from source at the pinned commit, each with whether and how it carries the token (header, query, none) and the file and line it was read from. The file's header no longer says these requests are left out

The differential tier's client run sends each 'player' request to jellyscale and holds the answer to the form: a media request with no token answers 401, one with a token 2xx, and a picture request 200 either way. Findroid's direct-play request is expected to answer 401, and a test fails if it stops doing so without the list changing

docs/status.md's client table gains, per client, whether its player sends the token on direct play, on HLS, on subtitles and on pictures, with 'read from source' or 'played on a device' beside each. Findroid's row says direct play fails with 401 and why. docs/access.md's section 'What a client must send' states the header and the query forms
docs/access.md's 'Stricter than Jellyfin' table names, for each row, the capture entry that observed Jellyfin's answer; a row with no observation says 'source only'
userStories.notes: No handler changes. Findroid builds its URL in JellyfinRepositoryImpl.kt:341-348 (013eb52) with getVideoStreamUrl(itemId, static = true, mediaSourceId). Swiftfin appends ApiKey itself (RemotePlaybackURL.swift:21-25). The lead drafts the upstream issue for Findroid from the client list and files it with the owner's OK. JS-075's ExoPlayer session should use a client this task shows sending its token, or a patched Findroid. Whether Jellyfin's anonymous stream really sends bytes on 12.4 is what the first criterion finds out: the attribute is missing in source, the handler was not run. Owner's decisions (2026-11-16, on Fable 5.2's access model, .results/access-model-fable-2026-11-16.md): pictures by id open to whoever holds the id, by name need a token; per-library access right after JS-033; a revoked or disabled user's running stream stops within 15 s; a viewer sees no other viewer's name; an administrator manages accounts but never browses, plays or reports as another user; a Policy field jellyscale does not enforce is refused when changed (400); 'may download' is honoured; operator keys are never users; no issue is filed on Findroid for now.

userStories.title: A playlist carries the token only when the request carried it in the URL
userStories.description: jellyscale writes the caller's token as ApiKey into every line of master.m3u8 and main.m3u8, however the request was authenticated (internal/api/transcode.go:99-104, internal/playback/spec.go:314-326). Fluster sends its token only in a header and refuses, by design, any playlist that carries a credential (its src-tauri/src/player/hls/session.rs:69-75, decision 0002), so it cannot play a jellyscale conversion at all (read from both sources, not run). jellyfin-web's player loads TranscodingUrl as a URL and needs the token in it. So the playlist follows the request: the token goes into its lines only when the request carried it in the query.
acceptanceCriteria: Observed first: compat/captures records what Jellyfin 12.4 writes in the lines of master.m3u8 and main.m3u8 when the master is requested with the token in the Authorization header and when with ApiKey in the query

A master or main playlist requested with the token only in a header (Authorization MediaBrowser, X-Emby-Authorization, X-Emby-Token or X-MediaBrowser-Token) carries no ApiKey, api_key or token in any line; every URI in it, requested with that same header and no query token, answers as today (the variant playlist, the init segment, every media segment)
Requested with ApiKey or api_key in the query, every line carries ApiKey as today; jellyfin-web's transcode e2e scenarios pass unchanged
A request that carries the token in both a header and the query is treated as a query request (lines keep ApiKey), so no client that relies on today's lines loses them
Every segment and playlist route still refuses a request with no token (JS-125's TestAccess unchanged)
A test sends the master with each of the four header spellings and fails if any line of the master or the variant playlist contains the token's value
docs/access.md ('What a client must send') and docs/transcoding.md say which requests get the token in playlist lines; JS-040 (signed URLs) notes that header requests already carry none
userStories.notes: Found 2026-11-16 while drafting Fluster issues (the owner wants Fluster first-class). Fluster also strips ApiKey from subtitle DeliveryUrls (gateway.ts:178-195); PlaybackInfo's TranscodingUrl and DeliveryUrls keep ApiKey here, because jellyfin-web loads them as URLs. Fewer tokens in URLs is also safer (DOMAINS invariant 17).
userStories.source: lead 2026-11-16, from the Fluster issue research

userStories.title: The integration tier fits its limits, and a queue run stops paying for waste
userStories.description: On 2026-11-16, 6 merge-queue runs were cancelled because the rest shard hit its 40-minute job limit (2417 s) and at least 3 failed because shard 0of4 hit go test's 30-minute limit (run 43892801970). test/shard-times.txt lacks 135 of main's 362 transcode tests, 1836 s on CI, the three slowest among them; each counts as 4.2 s. rest runs internal/api (1226 s) and cmd/jellyscale (630 s) in turn in one job. 13 jobs install ffmpeg from a mirror (7.5 to 13.8 runner-minutes a run; the step timed out in run 43909360415). test/e2e/failover.mjs waits out a 180 s timer after its last scenario (161 s). The differential tier fetches its jars from Maven Central every run (429 in run 43919042492).
acceptanceCriteria: test/shard-times.txt is made by test/shard-times.sh from the tests.json of at least three green merge-queue runs (its header names the run ids and says CI's runners) and holds every test that go test -tags integration -list finds in the packages test/shard.sh deals by test

test/shard.sh deals internal/api's tests by time as it deals internal/transcode's, so no shard is one package's serial run; test/check-shards.sh integration still fails when a test is in no shard or in two, and test/scripts_test.sh shows it for a second dealt package

test/scripts_test.sh fails, naming the shard, when the times in test/shard-times.txt for any shard add up to more than two thirds of the go test limit set in test/integration.sh (today 0of4 holds 29.2 minutes of tests against 30)

The integration job's summary prints each shard's test seconds and the line 'refresh test/shard-times.txt' when the slowest shard's are more than 1.25 times the fastest's; it is a notice and fails nothing
In the first three merge-queue runs after the change no integration job takes over 27 minutes (today 38.5 to 39.9) and none is cancelled or stopped by a time limit

ffmpeg, fontconfig and the font are installed from .deb files restored by actions/cache (keyed on the runner image version and the package list); on a hit the install step makes no request to an Ubuntu mirror and takes under 30 s in every job of a queue run; a miss installs as today and saves; the step that fails a job whose ffmpeg is not 6.1 is unchanged

test/e2e/failover.mjs ends when its last scenario has: in the failover shard's log under 5 s pass between 'shard 0/1: ran 5 of 5' and the conform line (today 161 s); a test with a stand-in replica that never exits still fails with 'the replica that got SIGTERM was still running 180 s later'
The jars test/sdkjvm/decode.sh needs are restored by actions/cache keyed on jars.txt; with the cache warm the differential shard makes no request to Maven Central
No file matching *_integration_test.go changes, and the tier's test count from go test -list is the same before and after
When lint-and-unit fails in a run, that run's integration, e2e, roles and differential jobs are cancelled at once (owner, 2026-11-16); the required checks still report failure
userStories.notes: Priority 1. As a stopgap in the first commit, raise the job limit to 50 minutes and go test's to 40 so the queue stops killing runs while the split lands; set them back to 30 and 40 in the last. Planned by Fable 5.2 (.results/test-time-fable-2026-11-16.md). Owner's decisions 2026-11-16: skip the media tiers for .claude/ and tasks/ changes with a guard test (JS-132); cancel media shards when lint-and-unit fails; the merge queue builds 2 entries (back to 3 once a run costs under ~150 runner-minutes and under a fifth of runs fail) with a 90-minute check timeout, set by the lead. 2026-11-16: four dealt shards could not meet 27 minutes (6953 s of dealt tests, 29 min each), so CI deals over five plus rest, and lint fails when a dealt shard's recorded tests pass 1500 s. The lead checks the first three queue runs after merge.

userStories.title: A runner runs several test processes side by side, each with its own Postgres
userStories.description: The integration tier idles: measured on four pinned cores, internal/transcode kept 0.69 of 4 CPUs busy (4887 s wall, 3364 CPU-s) and the 28 slowest tests of the other packages 0.18. The account runs 20 jobs at once (measured peak, held 96 minutes on 2026-11-16), so runner-minutes, not shards, bound the queue. Local runs on 2 cores / 4 threads: the 28 slowest rest tests as four processes in 420 s against 1510 s serial on CI, all passing; the 33 slowest transcode tests as three processes in 1390 s against 3486 s, one failure.
acceptanceCriteria: INTEGRATION_PROCS=n makes test/integration.sh start n Postgres containers on Docker-assigned ports and run n go test processes at once, each over its own share of the shard's tests (dealt by time by test/shard.sh), with its own JELLYSCALE_TEST_DATABASE_URL, TMPDIR and tests.json; test/scripts_test.sh, with stand-in docker and go, fails if a test is in two shares or in none, or if two processes are given one database URL

A failed test, a skipped test, a process that stops partway (a panic, go test's limit) or a count that does not add up to go test -list fails the shard and names the test, as today; a stand-in process that exits early fails the script test
No *_test.go file, test/e2e/*.mjs or file under test/differential changes, other than for a test named under the next criterion but one: the checks are the ones that ran before

Every mutant of test/mutant.py fails the tier side by side on the test it fails alone (test/mutant.sh <mutant> with INTEGRATION_PROCS set), and so do three transcode regressions the spec writer names from JS-066, JS-104 and JS-105, each shown failing alone and side by side

A test that fails side by side and passes alone is fixed at its cause (the interleaving forced, the count made independent of load) or listed in test/alone.txt with its reason and run in a process of its own; none is retried, skipped or given a longer bound. TestTheScanReadsNoMoreOfAFilmForItsImageTrackAndNothingThatGrowsWithTheFilm is the first to settle (it failed once in three processes on four logical CPUs, 2026-11-16)

On the queue the integration tier is at most five jobs; in ten consecutive merge-queue runs after the change no integration job takes over 20 minutes, the tier's jobs add up to at most 85 runner-minutes (today 137 to 140), and none of the ten fails on a test that passes when run alone
docs/testing.md says how the tier is split twice (jobs, then processes), how to run one process's share locally, and that a concurrency claim still needs its own real processes or contention
userStories.notes: The 20-minute and 85-runner-minute bounds come from local experiments, not from CI; if the first queue runs show a 4-vCPU runner cannot hold them at two processes for transcode and four for the rest, the lead restates them from those runs, never by removing or loosening a test. A Postgres per process, not a database per process: some transcode tests end backends chosen from pg_locks, which is cluster-wide. core: true. Planned by Fable 5.2 (.results/test-time-fable-2026-11-16.md). Owner's decisions 2026-11-16: skip the media tiers for .claude/ and tasks/ changes with a guard test (JS-132); cancel media shards when lint-and-unit fails; the merge queue builds 2 entries (back to 3 once a run costs under ~150 runner-minutes and under a fifth of runs fail) with a 90-minute check timeout, set by the lead. 2026-11-17: CI runs 0/4 to 3/4 at two processes and rest at four. Every mutant and the JS-066, JS-104 and JS-105 regressions fail side by side; the two access mutants that make Handler() panic stop the shard partway (named) and their declaration tests fail in lint-and-unit. The lead checks the ten queue runs after merge.

userStories.title: The slowest checks do less work for the same claim
userStories.description: After JS-130 CPU is what a runner lacks. The image burn-in kit encodes 640x360 films at 1280x720; a scratch run at the films' own size took three tests from 655 to 445 CPU-s with all passing. Four waits are not the claim: the two slow-database tests play a 90 s film through 1 s round trips (551 s) where the claim needs more than two leases; TestAProcessWithoutTheWorkerRoleWritesNothingToTheLibraries stops 18 processes one after another at 5 s each (98 s, 3 CPU-s); TestARegistryThatAnswersNotFoundHasTheTagAbsentAndIsWrittenTo takes 100 s on CI and 1.5 s locally; TestAWorkerStoppedPastItsLeaseAndTheStallLimitEndsItsJobCancelled repeats each shape three times to sample a race.
acceptanceCriteria: The image burn-in kit asks for 640x360, the size of every film it writes, in both places it sets a spec: newScanned/newScannedThrough (image_burn_kit_integration_test.go) and scannedByThePreviousRelease (image_burn_upgrade_integration_test.go); tests outside the kit keep the spec they ask for

Each of the 20 tests built on the kit's scannedFilm passes at 640x360 (the tests of image_burn_cues, _failures, _lookback, _reads and _runs, and the two of _upgrade), and none of their checks, byte bounds, thresholds or tolerances is removed or loosened

Each of those 20 is shown failing under a named one-line mutant of a right build at 1280x720 before the change and at 640x360 after it. Where the test's comment names a mutant, that mutant is used (a run that reads only the later packet, a run that begins after the cue); otherwise the mutant is the defect the test exists to catch. One mutant may serve several tests

TestASlowDatabaseSetBeforeTheClaimCostsNoJobItsLeaseOrItsWorker and TestASlowDatabaseCostsNoJobItsLeaseOrItsWorker keep every worker round trip at 1 s and keep every assertion they have: one row, one worker, one ffmpeg, no lease found run out, the job done, every segment stored. Only the film changes, to one whose job outlasts two leases and no more than six

Each slow-database test fails itself as a harness error when its job ended done inside two leases (20 s), counted from when the 1 s round trips were in force on the claimed job, not from the test's start. Each test logs that time, which is over 20 s and at most 60 s in every one of QA's CI-shaped runs

A keeper that gives its connect the renewal's bound fails TestASlowDatabaseSetBeforeTheClaimCostsNoJobItsLeaseOrItsWorker, and a renewal sent in two round trips fails TestASlowDatabaseCostsNoJobItsLeaseOrItsWorker. Each fails in every one of three runs and on the test's own assertions (the job not done, a lease run out, a second job or ffmpeg), not on the two-lease guard

TestAProcessWithoutTheWorkerRoleWritesNothingToTheLibraries starts its 18 processes (api, stream and api,stream, each with its 6 lists) so that all 18 are serving at the same time before any is stopped. It judges each process only after that process has exited, in a subtest named by its roles and list

A build in which a process without the worker role calls library.Sync fails all 18 subtests. A build in which only the api role calls it fails the 12 subtests with api and none of the 6 stream-only ones, so each write is laid to the process that made it

Before the registry stub changes, the cause of TestARegistryThatAnswersNotFoundHasTheTagAbsentAndIsWrittenTo's 100 s on CI is read from a queue run's log (gh run view --log) and quoted in the PR; the change to the stub addresses that observed cause

For each of MANIFEST_UNKNOWN and NAME_UNKNOWN, the stub refuses the write with a status docker push does not retry, the publish exits non-zero, and the stub records the attempted write. On the first queue run after the merge, the test takes under 10 s
A publish.sh that reads a 404 as a registry it cannot ask, and so pushes nothing, fails the registry test once for each of the two codes

TestAWorkerStoppedPastItsLeaseAndTheStallLimitEndsItsJobCancelled is four subtests, each run once and with no rounds: the worker alone and the worker with its ffmpeg, each once with the poll seeing the stop first and once with the heartbeat seeing it first

Each subtest forces its order from outside the worker process and confirms it from what the worker or the database recorded. It fails as a harness error if the other one saw the stop first. Each subtest still stops the worker past both the lease and the stall limit, and requires the job to end cancelled, never failed, and the ffmpeg to be gone

A build that ends failed a job the lease keeper cut (the keeper-cause arm of the job's context ending, worker.go) fails both heartbeat-first subtests, and a build whose upload ends the job failed on a lost lease fails both poll-first subtests. Each fails in every one of three runs. (Lead, 2026-11-17: the worker's own stall arm, stop("ffmpeg has stalled"), is unreachable after a stop past the lease, because the keeper cuts the job before any beat arrives; the PR says so.)
No product code changes: the diff touches only test files, test scripts, test fixtures and docs, and adds no test hook to non-test Go code
QA runs the two slow-database tests and the stall test under test/ffmpeg61.sh with JELLYSCALE_TEST_CPUS=0-1 and -count=3 on one database, and every run of each passes

Compare the tests.json of the last queue run before the merge with the first one after it: the seconds of the five named tests and the kit's 20 tests together are at least 500 s lower after (the lead checks this after the merge)
userStories.notes: Lowest of the four. Whether Docker's retries are the cause of the 100 s is unverified; observe it on a runner first. Planned by Fable 5.2 (.results/test-time-fable-2026-11-16.md). Owner's decisions 2026-11-16: skip the media tiers for .claude/ and tasks/ changes with a guard test (JS-132); cancel media shards when lint-and-unit fails; the merge queue builds 2 entries (back to 3 once a run costs under ~150 runner-minutes and under a fifth of runs fail) with a 90-minute check timeout, set by the lead. Built 2026-11-17 in OpenCode (Claude Code's weekly limit reached): refine and check on Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.2, spec, build and verify on Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5. The burn-in kit renders at 640x360; the slow-database tests play a 14 s film (jobs done 36-49 s after the slow round trips begin, two-lease guard); the 18 library processes serve at once, each on its own database; the registry stub refuses with 403 DENIED, which docker push does not retry (observed on classic dockerd 28.5.2: a 500 was retried five times, 50 s a push; the CI log cannot show it, since a passing test prints nothing); the stall test is four forced subtests (poll first by stopping the worker inside a Put held through JELLYSCALE_TEST_SLOWPUT). Mutants live in test/mutant.py, run by test/mutants.sh; test/scripts_test.sh checks each still applies. Criterion 14 reworded by the lead: the worker's own stall arm is unreachable after a stop past the lease. Criterion 17 (500 s less in a queue run's tests.json) is checked by the lead after merge. Checked after merge (queue runs 44099410515 before, 44232940797 after): the five named tests went from 781 s to 183 s and the image burn-in tests from 1119 s to 957 s, 759 s less in all; the registry test took 0.5 s on CI.

userStories.title: An AV1 copy whose keyframe index is found wrong goes on as a re-encode
userStories.description: JS-088 made a copy whose index is found wrong go on as an x264 or x265 encode cut on the playlist's layout, so the viewer never sees the failure. An AV1 copy still fails as before and the picture freezes mid-film, because no restart-safe AV1 encode was built; the workers' ffmpeg has SVT-AV1. PRODUCT.md says no codec is second-class, so the gap is closed here: an AV1 fallback that splices on the playlist's layout like the other two, or an H.264 fallback a client that played AV1 can take (with its own init, as JS-088 sends one), whichever the observation shows works in jellyfin-web.
acceptanceCriteria: Observed in jellyfin-web 12.4 (its hls.js 1.6.16) in Chromium and recorded beside compat/captures/segment-errors-12.4.md with the script that reproduces it: an AV1 copy's playlist whose later segments are H.264, each led by its own init, played forward across the change and then seeked back into an AV1 segment and forward across the change again; for each direction the record says the frames shown, video.error, whether a dialog shows and whether currentTime keeps its place

The fallback's codec follows that record and is the same for every AV1 copy: H.264 only if both directions showed frames with no video.error and no dialog, otherwise AV1 (SVT-AV1); the record names the choice and the checks below hold the build to it

In the e2e tier, jellyfin-web in Chromium plays an AV1 film with keyframes 5 to 7 s apart as a copy (VideoCodec=copy, CODECS av01), its index is found wrong, and the viewer reaches 30 s past the bad point with no Playback Error dialog, no /Videos/ request answered 400 or more, no playlist or segment request abandoned, no video.error, no corrupted frames, at least 480 of those 30 s' 720 frames shown, and currentTime never going back by more than 4 s or forward by more than 1 s; the index is then recorded dropped and a worker's ffmpeg encoded the picture

That holds in two scenarios, each on a film of its own, one 8-bit AV1 and one 10-bit: the viewer seeks into the bad segment before any job has reached it, and the job finds the index wrong while the viewer is still more than 4 s before the bad point on stored copy segments and then plays across it

With a real worker and ffmpeg, for an AV1 film whose copy layout differs from the 4 s grid in count and in every start after the first, fetched both with the stored segments first and with the bad segment first: every segment starts on a keyframe, starts within 0.05 s of the playlist's start and lasts within 0.1 s of its EXTINF, each fallback segment holds the frames of its length to within 1, and the segments together hold the film's frames with none skipped or played twice

Every segment answered after the fallback, the stored AV1 copy segments included, leads with the init segment of its own stream and decodes under it with no error; a fallback segment's init is of the codec the second criterion fixed

A fallback run begun at segment 1, at a middle segment and at the last one, as a restart begins, splices with the earlier segments of a run from the start: the same number of frames, frame times within 1 ms, audio packet times within 0.5 ms, no decoder warning across the join and the same init segment, at 24000/1001 and 25 fps, on Ubuntu 24.04's ffmpeg 6.1 and on ffmpeg 9

When the worker making an AV1 copy's fallback is killed mid-job, another worker makes the rest from the first missing segment and the waiting request is answered with no error status; the two workers' segments join as in the criterion before (invariant 22)
The fallback of a 4K AV1 copy (3840x2160) is 1920x1080, a wider one keeps its aspect ratio within 1080 lines, and a copy of 1080 lines or fewer keeps its size

The fallback's price is at least the CPU time (user plus system) its own ffmpeg command uses per second of film, measured for a 1080p and a 4K 24 fps AV1 source, and a tone-mapped one is priced no lower than the SDR one of the same source; docs/transcoding.md records the machine, the ffmpeg and encoder versions, the CPU and wall-clock figures (wall-clock no slower than the film plays) and the cost table's rows

One viewer of an AV1 copy that falls back and fetches at least 5 fallback segments raises jellyscale_playback_copy_fallbacks_total, summed over the stream replicas, by exactly 1 and gets one log line with item, source and reason; two viewers of the same AV1 copy raise it by exactly 2
A worker of the release before (output version 5) never claims an AV1 copy's fallback job: OutputVersion is raised, so the job waits for a worker that makes it (invariant 59)
userStories.notes: JS-088's docs say SVT-AV1 is present but a restart-safe AV1 encode is not built. Cost: an SVT-AV1 encode is CPU-heavy; measure before pricing.

userStories.title: An HDR copy's fallback keeps the picture's range
userStories.description: JS-088 and JS-133 make a copy whose keyframe index is found wrong go on as an encode of the copy's codec. The fallback's picture is always `format=yuv420p`, 8 bits with no colour tags, and a copy has no tone mapping (`Spec.ToneMap` is empty), so an HDR10 or HLG HEVC or AV1 copy, which is copied only to a client whose profile shows the range (master playlist `VIDEO-RANGE=PQ` or `HLG`), would go on mid-film as PQ or HLG samples squeezed into 8 bits and tagged as SDR: washed out or banded, the failure JS-088 exists to hide. Not observed yet (found reading internal/transcode/ffmpeg.go after JS-133). PRODUCT.md: no film is second-class, and an HDR viewer keeps HDR.
acceptanceCriteria: Recorded in compat/captures beside av1-fallback-12.4.md, with the commands that reproduce it, for an HDR10 HEVC copy and an HDR10 AV1 copy: what ffprobe says of the copy and of today's fallback of it, for the init segment and for the frames of each (pixel format and bit depth, primaries, transfer, matrix, range, mastering display and content light level), and whether today's fallback is tone mapped

Recorded there with the script that reproduces it, in jellyfin-web 12.4's hls.js 1.6.16 in Chromium: a 10-bit PQ copy's playlist whose later segments are today's fallback, and again with a 10-bit fallback carrying the copy's tags, each segment led by its own init, played forward across the change, then seeked back into a copy segment (a 10-bit init after an 8-bit one) and forward across it again; for each direction the frames shown, video.error, whether a dialog shows, whether currentTime keeps its place, and whether the colours Chrome draws of the same picture differ before and after the change; for AV1 always, and for HEVC where the observing browser plays it, otherwise marked not observed

The record names the format the fallback of an HDR copy takes, and the checks below hold the build to it: 10 bits with the copy's tags and no tone mapping, unless the player was seen to refuse that (video.error, a dialog or no frames in either direction), which goes to the owner and is not settled by the build sending another format

With a real worker and ffmpeg, on Ubuntu 24.04's ffmpeg 6.1 and on ffmpeg 9, the fallback of each of an HDR10 HEVC, HLG HEVC, HDR10 AV1 and HLG AV1 copy, and of an HDR10+ HEVC copy as its HDR10 picture, is 10 bits in the profile the master playlist's CODECS names (HEVC Main 10, AV1 profile 0 at 10 bits), and ffprobe shows the copy's own primaries, transfer, matrix and range for the fallback's init segment alone and for the frames of every fallback segment as it is answered (its init in front)

That fallback is the copy's own picture: its decoded frames are nearer the source's frames at the same times (scaled alike, at 10 bits) than the frames of the tone-mapped fallback today's build makes of the same film, and its ffmpeg command has no tone-mapping filter and no 8-bit pixel format on the way

The fallback of an SDR copy (8 or 10 bit; H.264, HEVC or AV1) and of an H.264 copy in any range has the ffmpeg arguments and the 8-bit picture it has today, and every JS-088 and JS-133 check passes as written, bar those that pin OutputVersion's number and the hashes that follow from it

A fallback run of an HDR10 HEVC copy and of an HDR10 AV1 copy begun at segment 1, at a middle segment and at the last, as a restart begins, splices with the earlier segments of a run from the start: a byte-identical init segment (so the same bit depth and tags), the same number of frames, frame times within 1 ms, audio packet times within 0.5 ms and no decoder warning across the join that the run from the start lacks, on Ubuntu 24.04's ffmpeg 6.1 and on ffmpeg 9

When the worker process making an HDR copy's fallback is killed mid-job, another worker process makes the rest from the first missing segment, the waiting request is answered with no error status, and the two workers' segments join as in the criterion before (invariant 22), for HEVC and for AV1; it holds three runs in a row on two CPUs under ffmpeg 6.1 (test/ffmpeg61.sh, JELLYSCALE_TEST_CPUS=0-1, -count=3)

The price (Spec.Cost) of an HDR copy's fallback is at least the CPU time (user plus system) its own ffmpeg command uses per second of film, measured through a worker for a 1080p and a 4K 24 fps HDR10 source, for HEVC and for AV1, on ffmpeg 6.1 and on ffmpeg 9; docs/transcoding.md records the machine, the ffmpeg and encoder versions, the CPU and wall-clock figures (wall-clock no slower than the film plays) and the cost table's rows, and the 4K copy's fallback is 1920x1080 as before

A worker of the release before (output version 6) never claims the fallback job of an HDR copy: OutputVersion is raised (invariant 59), so no 8-bit or tone-mapped segment is stored under the new fallback's hash

In the e2e tier, jellyfin-web in Chromium plays an HDR10 film with keyframes 5 to 7 s apart as a copy (VideoCodec=copy, master VIDEO-RANGE=PQ; the HEVC film when E2E_HEVC=1, the AV1 one otherwise, as in CI), the job finds its index wrong while the viewer is more than 4 s before the bad point on stored copy segments, and the viewer reaches 30 s past it with no Playback Error dialog, no /Videos/ request answered 400 or more, no playlist or segment request abandoned, no video.error, no corrupted frames, at least 480 of those 30 s' 720 frames shown, and currentTime never going back by more than 4 s or forward by more than 1 s

In that scenario the index is then recorded dropped, a worker's ffmpeg encoded the picture with the copy's codec, and a fallback segment as the browser was answered it is 10 bits with the copy's transfer (PQ), so the scenario fails on today's 8-bit fallback

A Dolby Vision copy whose base layer is HDR10 (profiles 8.1 and 7 in HEVC, 10.1 in AV1) or HLG (8.4) falls back at 10 bits with its base layer's primaries, transfer, matrix and range, as in the fourth criterion, and one whose base layer is SDR (8.2) as an SDR copy does; or, for each kind left out, docs/transcoding.md names it, says why and says what the viewer gets instead, and a check holds the build to what the docs say

docs/transcoding.md says what an HDR copy's fallback keeps (10 bits, primaries, transfer, matrix, range) and what the record shows it does not (HDR10 mastering display and content light level, HDR10+ and Dolby Vision dynamic metadata, lines above 1080), each loss written as a gap

userStories.title: Browser-engine clients connect from any origin, without credentials
userStories.description: Fluster (a Tauri WebView) and any web client hosted on another origin fail before sign-in: API answers carry no Access-Control-Allow-Origin and preflights answer 404 (issue #202). D-016: open to any origin, never with credentials; tokens travel only in headers or the query, so no other site can make a viewer's browser send one.
acceptanceCriteria: Observed first: a rerunnable capture in compat/captures of a real Jellyfin 12.4 records the status and every Access-Control-*, Vary and Allow header it answers, for two different origins and for no Origin, to: a GET of an open route; a GET of a viewer route with a token and with none; a ranged GET of a film; a preflight for the sign-in (POST, asking authorization and content-type); a preflight asking range; one asking DELETE and one asking PATCH; one asking a header outside the six below; and a GET and a preflight for an unserved path

Every difference between that capture and what jellyscale answers to the same requests (status, Access-Control-*, Vary) is in compat/differences.yaml with its reason, and a check asks jellyscale the capture's requests and fails on a difference that is not listed

In Chromium, a page served from an origin other than the server's reads GET /System/Info/Public, reads a wrong password as a 401 (not as a failed connection), signs in with POST /Users/AuthenticateByName (JSON body), and lists the libraries and one library's films, sending Authorization: MediaBrowser on every request and its token in no URL; the server is two api replicas and a stream replica as separate processes behind the router, and each of these requests is answered by an api replica

The same page, its token still only in the Authorization header, direct plays a film from bytes it fetched by script: a request for a range in the middle of the file answers 206 with exactly those bytes, the page itself reads Content-Range, Accept-Ranges and Content-Length from the answer, and the picture advances before and after a seek; the stream replica answers each request and its preflight

The same page plays a film that transcodes, sending the Authorization header on the master playlist, the main playlist and every segment (ApiKey taken off the TranscodingUrl): time advances, and after a seek beyond what was buffered a segment at the new place is fetched and time advances there; the stream replica answers each request and its preflight
Each of those steps is shown to fail on today's build by itself: the open read, the sign-in, and, given a token obtained outside the page, the browse, the direct play and the transcode

Each of the 92 routes of compat/endpoints.yaml (the 4 under /jellyscale/v1/ and GET /socket included), asked on a process that has only the route's role (79 on api alone, 13 on stream alone), answers a preflight from each of tauri://localhost, http://tauri.localhost, https://tauri.localhost and an https web origin, 368 in all, with a 2xx that allows that origin, the route's method and all six of Authorization, X-Emby-Authorization, X-Emby-Token, X-MediaBrowser-Token, Content-Type and Range; a path in another letter case or with a trailing slash is answered as the route itself is, checked on every route of compat/endpoints.yaml, not one (D-019)

Each of the six headers is allowed when asked alone, together, in any order and in any letter case, and Authorization is allowed by name (a browser does not take `*` for it); the 5 DELETE and 2 PATCH routes are allowed by name, each of the 8 paths with two methods allows both, HEAD is allowed wherever GET is served, and a path in another letter case or with a trailing slash is answered as the route itself is

Every answer of a route to a request that carries an Origin allows that origin, whatever the answer: 200, 204, 206, the 401 of no token, an unknown token and a wrong password, a handler's 404, a 416, and a 5xx from a store failure; the query spellings (ApiKey, api_key) need no preflight and their answers are readable the same way

A picture asked from one origin, from another and with no Origin is right for each from a shared cache: the allowed origin is `*`, or every answer of the route, with an Origin or without, carries Vary: Origin

Wherever an answer carries Content-Range or Accept-Ranges (the direct play, the download and the subtitle and font files, on 200, 206 and HEAD), a page on another origin can read them and Content-Length

A preflight needs no token and no Postgres: it is answered the same with no credential, a valid token and an unknown one, for an id that exists and one that does not, by a server with no database, and, on an api replica and on a stream replica, while Postgres is stopped (answered before Postgres returns, having sent it no statement); a viewer in the snapshot who plays from another origin with a header token still gets each segment or range and its preflight, with the origin allowed, through the outage

A preflight carries no information about the server and does nothing: no body, no header whose value differs between two servers (name, id, version) or with what the database holds, no handler run (a preflight for POST /Sessions/Logout or DELETE /Videos/ActiveEncodings changes nothing, even with a token on it), and one for a served route is not logged as an unknown route

Nothing an operator owns is opened: a GET with an Origin and a preflight for /healthz and for /readyz (ready, and 503) on an api and on a stream process, and for /metrics on the metrics listener of an api, a stream and a worker process, carry no Access-Control-* header, and answer the status and body they answer today
No answer carries Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: none of the 368 preflights, no answer of the 92 routes with a token or without, no error answer, and none to a request that sends a Cookie header

A check driven from the route table (so a new route is covered) fails if any route's answer, with a token, without one, or to a preflight, carries Set-Cookie, and a valid token sent only in a Cookie header, under each spelling's name, is answered 401 `unauthorized`; the check is shown to fail on a build that sets a cookie
DOMAINS.md has an invariant that a viewer's token never travels in a cookie and no route sets one, naming that check and binding JS-039 and JS-122 by name
No route's access changes: the open list is the same 11 routes, and each of the 81 viewer routes asked from another origin with no token still answers 401 `unauthorized`

jellyfin-web served by jellyscale and the differential tier's clients get the status, the body and every header other than Access-Control-* and Vary that they got before; the browse, play, subtitles, failover and transcode gates and the differential tier pass with no existing scenario, request or allowlist entry changed

docs/access.md says a preflight is open to anyone and why (a browser sends it with no token, before any request that carries one in a header), that any origin may call the API and media routes, why that does not open a viewer's account (no cookie: a page can only use a token it already holds), what it does expose (on a server reachable only on a private network, a web page in a viewer's browser can read the open routes and the result of a sign-in attempt), and that /healthz, /readyz and /metrics are not opened; its sentence that every other method and path gets the catch-all's 404 is made true again
docs/status.md's Fluster row says what was shown (Chromium on another origin; preflights for the three WebView origins) and that Fluster itself has not been run, naming JS-075 (D-019)
userStories.notes: D-019: the Fluster record moved to JS-075; shipped on Chromium cross-origin and preflight evidence.
